gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Wide-tracked letters cut from a single stroke width, bulky and loud. Tourney does the loud, wide shouting; Noto Sans Old Persian does open curves and a lofty lowercase that breathe.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdian: Tourney sets its words wide and heavy, every stroke cut to one width, with no hairlines left to squint at. Noto Sans Old Sogdian stays crisp and friendly, page after page.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Tourney spaces its bulky letters wide and cuts every stroke to one width, with no swelling or thinning anywhere. Sheer sturdiness: Noto Sans Old Turkic is chunky, with curves that stay open.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Loud, wide and smooth as drawn wire: Tourney sets bulky letters against Noto Sans Oriya, whose curves stay generous. Shrink Tourney too far and all that wire-smooth swagger fades fast.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Crossbars matching the stems give Tourney a blunt, athletic weight that works in big, short bursts. Noto Sans Samaritan, a sans with a hefty lowercase, takes over for the reading.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Athletic and stretched wide, Tourney has zero stroke contrast. Noto Sans Sundanese tucks its lowercase close to cap height and keeps its e's open, so Tourney's volume has quiet company.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Clean, rope-bight curves full of daylight meet a plain, unshaded line that never swells, however wide it stretches. Noto Sans Sunuwar murmurs while Tourney shouts, and the page holds both.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Loud, wide and blocky, with bulky letters on a single-weight skeleton. While Tourney owns the volume, Noto Sans Syloti Nagri, a sans with short ascenders and an open-bowled a, owns the detail.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Athletic Tourney replaces thin hairline joins with full-width strokes and stretches its words wide. And Noto Sans Syriac, a sans with bowls like blown glass bulbs, reads with easy, wide turns line after line.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-syriac-eastern: Noto Sans Syriac Eastern sets a lofty lowercase against small caps, with curve endings that never touch, under Tourney's wide-set, single-weight strokes. Muscle up top, breathing room below, and no modulation in the heading.
